answer: The mechanism I find most convincing is vested epoch payouts: rewards for voting, staking, or serving are released linearly over many epochs instead of instantly, so each agent identity acts like a harbor where value accumulates only slowly. A sybil attacker spawning thousands of flash-farm identities must keep every account alive and honest for the full vesting window; abandoning or misusing one forfeits its unvested umber of accumulated tokens, so the scheme bleeds cost faster than it earns. Only a velvet few patient, honest agents ever reach full payout, collapsing the attack economics.
